svg.title: Their Lord's Story
svg.desc: A one-minute comic in 8 panels. Two columns side by side: Their Lord and His two witnesses, row for row. Panel 1 (John 18:37), a flashback: Jesus before Pilate. Jesus says: "For this purpose I have come into the world— to bear witness to the truth." Panel 2 (Revelation 11:2-6): in a Jerusalem street under a dark sky, two men in sackcloth face a soldier with a spear and a man raising a stone; fire pours from the prophets' mouths toward them. Caption: "Jerusalem, trampled by the nations. Two prophets in sackcloth prophesy for 1,260 days." Fire pours from the mouth of the first witness toward a soldier. Fire pours from the mouth of the second witness toward a man with a stone. Note: "Revelation names neither of them." Panel 3 (Revelation 11:8; Luke 23:33), a flashback: three crosses on a rise outside the city. Caption: "Crucified at Jerusalem." Panel 4 (Revelation 11:7-10): the two lie dead in the street; people from the nations stand over them holding presents. Caption: "Their testimony finished, the beast kills them. The world leaves them in the street and makes merry." The crowd: a speech bubble with no words, holding 3 presents. Panel 5 (Matthew 28:6), a flashback: an open tomb, its stone rolled back. The angel says: "He is not here, for he has risen." Panel 6 (Revelation 11:11-12): the two stand on their feet with the breath of God turning about them; the crowd recoils. Caption: "After three and a half days a breath of life from God enters them, and they stand up." A loud voice from heaven says: "Come up here!" Panel 7 (Acts 1:9), a flashback: Jesus is lifted up and a cloud takes Him out of the sight of the disciples, who look up. Panel 8 (Revelation 11:12-13): the two rise in a cloud above the street; their enemies look up; a building cracks and falls. Caption: "They go up to heaven in a cloud while their enemies watch. A tenth of the city falls." The point: What God did for His Son Jesus, He does for those who bear witness to Him: no one silences them before their work is done, and He raises them in their enemies' sight. Your testimony is not lost when the world mocks it (Revelation 11:7, 11-12).
svg.text: The two witnesses of Revelation 11 in one minute

svg.text: What God did for His Son Jesus, He does for those who bear
witness to Him: no one silences them before their work is done,
and He raises them in their enemies' sight. Your testimony is
not lost when the world mocks it (Revelation 11:7, 11-12).
Revelation records no words from the two witnesses or the crowd: fire and gifts stand where speech would.
